subject.title: [Bug]: browser navigation-guard explicit hostname allowlist broken by SSRF loopback tightening (#100835)

question: Should browser navigation exact-host allowlist entries continue to allow non-localhost hostnames that resolve to loopback, or should the post-100835 SSRF hardening retire that behavior?
rationale: Both outcomes change a security boundary: preserving the old behavior restores an operator-declared browser exception, while retiring it keeps the newly accepted fail-closed protection against loopback rebinding.

options.title: Preserve tightened boundary
options.body: Retire the custom loopback-alias contract for browser navigation and keep tests/docs aligned with explicit localhost, loopback literals, or private-network opt-in.

options.title: Approve scoped browser exception
options.body: Allow exact browser allowlist entries to cover the approved loopback case while continuing to reject metadata and link-local DNS answers, with focused tests and proof.

options.title: Defer to broader SSRF design
options.body: Keep this issue open until the related private-network confirmation and browser SSRF policy model are decided together.

recommendation.title: Preserve tightened boundary
recommendation.body: Retire the custom loopback-alias contract for browser navigation and keep tests/docs aligned with explicit localhost, loopback literals, or private-network opt-in.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent browser/CDP SSRF policy history and was the maintainer landing the related hardening PR.
